title: Answer a technical interview with evidence
summary: Giải thích một technical decision, contribution, trade-off và measured result.

sections.title: Your mission
sections.body: An interviewer asks about a production decision you personally influenced.

sections.title: Candidate notes
sections.content: Synthetic training artifact — non-production. Campaign launch in two weeks; API p95 latency 1.8s; target below 700ms; you profiled the request and found N+1 queries; options were caching or batching; you chose batching because caching added invalidation risk under the deadline and batching removed repeated reads. The cost was up to 25ms of batch-formation delay, and partial failures required mapping item-level errors back to the original requests. You added load tests; p95 became 520ms and DB load fell 28%.

expressions.meaning: Frame the constraint before comparing options.
expressions.example: Given the two-week deadline, I compared caching with batching.
alternatives: With ___ as the main constraint, I evaluated ___ and ___.

expressions.meaning: State a decision, rationale and acknowledged cost.
expressions.example: I chose batching because it removed repeated reads, although it added batch-formation delay.
alternatives: I selected ___ because ___; the trade-off was ___.

expressions.example: The change moved p95 latency from 1.8 seconds to 520 milliseconds.
alternatives: After the change, ___ fell from ___ to ___.

exercises.question: Which phrase proves personal contribution?
options: The team worked very hard and improved latency before the campaign started.
I profiled the queries, proposed batching and added load tests.
correctAnswer: I profiled the queries, proposed batching and added load tests.
exercises.explanation: It names decisions and actions owned by the candidate rather than attributing the result vaguely to the team.

exercises.question: Which cost must the candidate acknowledge when recommending batching?
options: Caching no longer needs invalidation, so the team can remove every monitoring alert.
Up to 25ms of batch-formation delay and item-level partial-failure handling.
Load tests become unnecessary once batching is deployed.
correctAnswer: Up to 25ms of batch-formation delay and item-level partial-failure handling.
exercises.explanation: The notes supply both the bounded delay and the extra work needed to map partial failures to original requests.

exercises.question: Why did batching fit the deadline better than caching?
options: It addressed repeated reads without adding cache invalidation risk.
It guaranteed that every request would succeed even during a full database outage.
It removed the need to measure p95 latency.
correctAnswer: It addressed repeated reads without adding cache invalidation risk.
exercises.explanation: The decision should connect the diagnosed N+1 pattern and deadline constraint to the chosen option without claiming guarantees.

performanceTask.title: Tell the decision story
performanceTask.scenario: Answer: Tell me about a technical decision you made under a deadline.
performanceTask.baselinePrompt: Speak for 90–120 seconds from the notes without model/chunks.
performanceTask.performancePrompt: In English, speak for 90–120 seconds: context, options and constraint, your decision, its cost and mitigation, measured result and reflection.
performanceTask.modelResponse: Two weeks before the campaign launch, API p95 latency was 1.8 seconds against a target below 700 milliseconds. I needed an option that could meet the target without creating avoidable risk under that deadline. I profiled the request and found an N-plus-one query path. I then compared caching with batching. Caching could reduce repeated reads, but it would add invalidation risk; batching addressed the repeated reads directly, so I chose batching. The cost was up to twenty-five milliseconds of batch-formation delay. I mitigated the partial-failure cost by mapping each item-level error back to its original request. I also added load tests so the decision had a measurable verification step. After the change, p95 latency fell to 520 milliseconds and database load fell by twenty-eight percent. That result met the latency target. Looking back, I would add query-count alerts earlier.
performanceTask.retryPrompt: Trong 90–120 giây, dùng database migration case mới và làm rõ option, constraint, rationale và cost.
performanceTask.transferPrompt: Trong 90–120 giây và không xem model/chunks, explain a decision that reduced deployment failures.
performanceTask.reviewPrompt: Trong 90–120 giây, answer a new technical-decision question about build performance.

artifacts.title: Decision facts
artifacts.content: Synthetic training artifact — non-production. Campaign launch in two weeks; p95 latency 1.8s; target below 700ms; you profiled the request and found N+1 queries; options were caching or batching; you chose batching because caching added invalidation risk under the deadline and batching removed repeated reads. Cost: batching added up to 25ms of batch-formation delay. Mitigation: map item-level errors back to their original requests when partial failures occur. You added load tests; p95 became 520ms and DB load fell 28%.

artifacts.title: Migration facts
artifacts.content: Synthetic training artifact — non-production. A 900GB table had a 20-minute maintenance window; options were big-bang or dual-write; you chose dual-write because a big-bang migration exceeded the window; cutover downtime was 90 seconds. Cost: temporary write-path complexity. Mitigation: put the dual-write path behind a feature flag, compare both paths during migration, and remove the old path after cutover validation.

artifacts.title: Release facts
artifacts.content: Synthetic training artifact — non-production. Deployment failure rate was 14%; options were a manual checklist or automated canary gate; you chose the canary because release pressure required a repeatable gate; failures fell to 3%. Cost: rollout took 8 minutes longer. Mitigation: reserve the extra time in the release window and automate the canary gate.

artifacts.title: Build facts
artifacts.content: Synthetic training artifact — non-production. CI took 24 minutes; options were larger runners or test sharding; the budget ruled out permanent larger runners; you chose sharding; CI fell to 11 minutes. Cost: flaky-test isolation became more complex. Mitigation: tag shard ownership and quarantine confirmed flaky tests while their owners repair them.

rubric.label: Complete decision story
rubric.description: Connects context, options or constraint, decision, result and reflection.

rubric.label: Decision rationale
rubric.description: Uses the current evidence packet to explain why the chosen option fit the stated constraint.

rubric.label: Trade-off and mitigation
rubric.description: Uses the current evidence packet to state its supplied trade-off cost and explain only the supplied mitigation.

rubric.label: Measured evidence
rubric.description: Uses the current packet's concrete result and frames any lesson as personal reflection.

audio.text: P ninety-five fell to five hundred and twenty milliseconds.
The trade-off was two extra deployment steps.
The deadline ruled out a full rewrite.
Given the deadline, I compared caching with batching.

training.question: What is compared?
training.feedback: Given the deadline makes the constraint explicit.

audio.text: I chose batching because it removed the root cause.

training.question: Why batching?
options: It was the easiest option for the team

audio.text: The result was lower latency and lower database load.

training.question: How many outcomes?
training.feedback: Keep final sounds in results and costs.

audio.text: The benefit was safety, but rollout took longer.

training.question: What structure is used?
training.feedback: Pause before but to expose the cost.

audio.text: I profiled the request and added load tests.

training.question: What is this evidence?
training.feedback: Use I plus specific action verbs.

audio.text: Looking back, I would add alerts earlier.
I selected request batching instead of a cache.
P ninety-five fell from one point eight seconds to five hundred and twenty milliseconds.
Database load fell by twenty-eight percent.
Looking back, I would add query-count alerts earlier.

pronunciationCues.articulatoryCue: Nhấn CHOSE/SELECTED và hai option; giảm nhẹ từ nối.
pronunciationCues.meaningRisk: Nếu option không nổi bật, interviewer không biết quyết định cụ thể là gì.

pronunciationCues.articulatoryCue: Tách before | after và đọc rõ đơn vị milliseconds/percent.
pronunciationCues.meaningRisk: Mất đơn vị hoặc contrast làm measured evidence sai nghĩa.
